question:
A 62-year-old male patient with a history of hypertension and dyslipidemia is in the intensive care unit
(ICU) following an open reduction and internal fixation of a right femur fracture sustained in a motor
vehicle accident. On postoperative day 3, he experienced transient hypotension due to Staphylococcus
aureus bacteremia, requiring vasopressor support for 24 hours. He is currently on parenteral
vancomycin, with negative repeat blood cultures and a normal echocardiogram. He no longer requires
vasopressors and is preparing for transfer out of the ICU. The patient has an indwelling Foley catheter
placed during surgery. The nurse observes slightly cloudy urine in the catheter bag. The patient reports
7/10 pain in the right leg but denies fever, chills, flank pain, or abdominal pain. His vital signs include a
temperature of 36.6■C, heart rate of 90 beats per minute, and blood pressure of 105/71 mm Hg.
Abdominal examination is unremarkable. Urinalysis reveals cloudy yellow urine with a pH of 6.0
(reference range: 5.0–9.0), specific gravity of 1.020 (1.001–1.035), 25–50 white cells per high-power
field (reference range: 0–2), 6–10 red cells per high-power field (0–2), 2+ bacteria, and no nitrites,

protein, or leukocyte esterase. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Replace the urinary catheter, repeat urinalysis with urine culture, and start empiric
ciprofloxacin (B) Replace the urinary catheter, and monitor for fever or other systemic signs of infection
(C) Continue parenteral vancomycin, and replace the urinary catheter (D) Remove the urinary catheter,
and perform a voiding trial (E) Discontinue vancomycin, and initiate oral nitrofurantoin (F) Perform a
cystoscopy to evaluate for bladder pathology (G) Start empiric trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and
continue the urinary catheter (H) Start empiric ceftriaxone, and discontinue the urinary catheter (I)
Obtain blood cultures, and start empiric meropenem (J) Send a urine culture, and start empiric
ciprofloxacin now
 A. Start empiric trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and continue the urinary catheter
B. Replace the urinary catheter, and monitor for fever or other systemic signs of infection
C. Continue parenteral vancomycin, and replace the urinary catheter
D. Discontinue vancomycin, and initiate oral nitrofurantoin
E. Perform a cystoscopy to evaluate for bladder pathology
F. Remove the urinary catheter, and perform a voiding trial
G. Obtain blood cultures, and start empiric meropenem
H. Send a urine culture, and start empiric ciprofloxacin now
I. Start empiric ceftriaxone, and discontinue the urinary catheter
J. Replace the urinary catheter, repeat urinalysis with urine culture, and start empiric ciprofloxacin
